title: HYDRAULIC PERFORMANCE OF FLEXIBLE DRIP IRRIGATION LATERALS UNDER VARIABLE OPERATING PRESSURES

HYDRAULIC PERFORMANCE OF FLEXIBLE DRIP IRRIGATION LATERALS UNDER VARIABLE OPERATING PRESSURES

ABSTRACT

This article investigates the improvement of hydraulic calculation methods for 16 mm diameter flexible drip irrigation pipes used in drip irrigation systems. The main objective of the study is to determine, based on field experiments, the variation patterns of head loss, specific hydraulic resistance, equivalent hydraulic roughness, and flow velocity in flexible drip irrigation pipes. The experiments were conducted in three field sites with different agrotechnical and operational conditions. During the measurements, the pressure difference between the inlet and outlet sections of the pipe, the flow rate discharged from the emitters, the flow velocity along the pipe length, and the field slope were determined. Based on the obtained data, the hydraulic parameters were calculated. According to the results of the study, the average specific hydraulic resistance coefficient of the 16 mm diameter flexible drip irrigation pipes was 21.1×10⁵ s²/m⁶. When the pressure increased within the range of 1.0–1.2 bar, the specific hydraulic resistance increased from 18.22×10⁵ s²/m⁶ to 24.43×10⁵ s²/m⁶. The relationship between specific hydraulic resistance and pressure was expressed by the regression equation A = 17.98p¹·⁴³, with a coefficient of determination of R² = 0.94. The pressure-dependent variation of equivalent hydraulic roughness was described by the equation Δ = 0.0304p⁵·⁹³, for which the coefficient of determination was R² = 0.95. In addition, the decrease in the average flow velocity along the pipe length was expressed by the equation υ = -0.9098l + 90.768, with R² = 0.999. The obtained results indicate that assuming hydraulic resistance and equivalent hydraulic roughness as constant values in flexible drip irrigation pipes may not provide sufficient accuracy. Therefore, in the hydraulic calculation of such pipes, operating pressure, pipe deformation, the hydraulic effect of the inner surface, and the decrease in flow rate along the pipe length should be considered jointly.
